s.en: execute a command as another user (root by default)
s.es: ejecuta un comando con los privilegios de otro usuario (por defecto root)

syn: sudo -h | -K | -k | -V ⏎ sudo -v [-ABkNnS] [-g group] [-h host] [-p prompt] [-u user] ⏎ sudo -l [-ABkNnS] [-g group] [-h host] [-p prompt] [-U user] [-u user] [command [arg ...]] ⏎ sudo [-ABbEHnPS] [-C num] [-D directory] [-g group] [-h host] [-p prompt] [-R directory] [-r role] [-t type] [-T timeout] [-u user] [VAR=value] [-i | -s] [command [arg ...]] ⏎ sudoedit [-ABkNnS] [-C num] [-D directory] [-g group] [-h host] [-p prompt] [-R directory] [-r role] [-t type] [-T timeout] [-u user] file ...

p.es: El comando (y sus argumentos) que se ejecutará con privilegios.
p.en: The command (and its arguments) to run with privileges.

o.es: Ejecuta como ese usuario en vez de root.
o.en: Run as that user instead of root.
Run with that primary group.

o.es: Abre una shell de login como el usuario destino (entorno completo, cambia al directorio personal).
o.en: Run a login shell as the target user (full environment, goes to their home).

o.es: Abre una shell como el usuario destino sin cambiar de directorio.
o.en: Run a shell as the target user without changing directory.

o.es: Conserva las variables de entorno del usuario actual.
o.en: Preserve the user's environment.

o.es: Pone HOME al directorio personal del usuario destino.
o.en: Set HOME to the target user's home directory.

o.es: Invalida la contraseña recordada: la pedirá de nuevo.
o.en: Invalidate the cached credentials: ask for the password again.

o.es: Elimina del todo la marca de tiempo de credenciales.
o.en: Remove the timestamp entirely.

o.es: Lista qué comandos tienes permitidos con sudo.
o.en: List the allowed (and forbidden) commands for the user.

o.es: Renueva la autenticación sin ejecutar ningún comando.
o.en: Update the user's cached credentials, without running a command.

o.es: Ejecuta el comando en segundo plano.
o.en: Run the command in the background.

o.es: No pide contraseña: falla si hace falta.
o.en: Avoid prompting the user for input of any kind.

o.es: Lee la contraseña de la entrada estándar (¡no la dejes en el historial!).
o.en: Write the prompt to standard error and read the password from standard input.

o.es: Edita archivos de forma segura (equivale a sudoedit).
o.en: Edit one or more files instead of running a command.

o.es: Pide la contraseña con un programa gráfico externo.
o.en: Use a helper program for password prompting.

o.es: Cambia el texto que pide la contraseña.
o.en: Use a custom password prompt.

o.es: Ejecuta en el host indicado (con sudoers por host).
o.en: Run the command on a host other than the local one.
Ring the bell as part of the password prompt when a terminal is present. This option has no effect if an askpass program is used.

Close all file descriptors greater than or equal to num before executing a command. Values less than three are not permitted. By default, sudo will close all open file descriptors other than standard input, standard output, and standard error when executing a command.
Run the command in the specified directory instead of the current working directory. The security policy may return an error if the user does not have permission to specify the working directory.
Do not update the user's cached credentials, even if the user successfully authenticates. Unlike the -k flag, existing cached credentials are used if they are valid.

Preserve the invoking user's group vector unaltered. By default, the sudoers policy will initialize the group vector to the list of groups the target user is a member of. The real and effective group-IDs, however, are still set to match the target user.

Change to the specified root directory (see chroot(8)) before running the command. The security policy may return an error if the user does not have permission to specify the root directory. This option is deprecated and will be removed in a future version of sudo.
Run the command with an SELinux security context that includes the specified role.
Run the command with an SELinux security context that includes the specified type. If no type is specified, the default type is derived from the role.
Used in conjunction with the -l option to list the privileges for user instead of for the invoking user. The security policy may restrict listing other users' privileges.

Used to set a timeout for the command. If the timeout expires before the command has exited, the command will be terminated. The security policy may restrict the user's ability to set timeouts. The sudoers policy requires that user-specified timeouts be explicitly enabled.

Print the sudo version string as well as the version string of any configured plugins. If the invoking user is already root, the -V option will display the options passed to configure when sudo was built; plugins may display additional information such as default options.
